speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of steroid use, significant weight loss, and progressive unilateral weakness, I need to rule out a thoracic outlet syndrome or a mass effect like Pancoast tumor. Do you have any shoulder pain, night sweats, or difficulty swallowing?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness in the right arm. I also have Decreased sensation in the right arm, Dull aching and burning pain in the right arm, Significant weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the combination of progressive right arm weakness, sensory loss, burning pain, and significant weight loss, I am highly suspicious of a Pancoast tumor or other malignancy. REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Diabetes Social history: Drinks 2-7 alcoholic beverages per day. Has smoked 2 packs of cigarettes per day since he was 25. Uses anabolic steroids.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies recent fevers, changes in vision, difficulty speaking, or changes in balance. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Multiple sclerosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: Multiple sclerosis typically presents with bilateral or multifocal neurological deficits, not isolated unilateral arm symptoms with significant weight loss. I need to evaluate for structural lesions like a Pancoast tumor or cervical spine pathology. REQUEST TEST: MRI_Chest

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the chest MRI is normal, the issue likely lies in the cervical spine or peripheral nerves, possibly exacerbated by steroid use. REQUEST TEST: MRI_Cervical_Spine

speaker: Doctor
text: Since structural causes in the chest and cervical spine have been ruled out, I suspect a peripheral nerve entrapment or polyneuropathy exacerbated by your diabetes and steroid use. REQUEST TEST: EMG_Nerve_Conduction_Study

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal imaging and EMG results, I must reconsider the earlier suggestion of Multiple Sclerosis despite the atypical presentation. REQUEST TEST: MRI_Brain

speaker: Doctor
text: All structural and peripheral nerve tests are normal, yet the previous doctor suggested Multiple Sclerosis. Do you have any history of visual disturbances, bladder dysfunction, or episodes of numbness in other body parts?

text: With all structural and peripheral nerve tests normal, I am ruling out MS due to the lack of multifocal lesions.
